description: We are The Space Maniacs, a multidisciplinary crew building an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer. Our platform puts young cadets in the pilot's seat through simulated mission scenarios, interactive problem-solving, and real-time feedback from an AI Mission Control companion. Our goal is to bridge the gap between textbook astronomy and hands-on astronaut training - making STEM accessible, immersive, and unforgettable for future explorers.
summary: Project Little Astronaut is a browser game that helps young learners explore the trade-offs behind a space outpost. Players keep life support powered, grow food, manage radiation risk, and decide when science is worth the cost. A visual tour introduces four stations, and a guided first decision teaches the controls before free exploration. Every action advances a turn and produces a clear explanation of what changed. Players can replay another choice from the same starting conditions, rewind, and explain their reasoning to an in-game cadet. Missions offer three difficulty levels, multiple saved games, and explicit win or loss reasons. NASA resources ground the science concepts; the game's resource numbers are simplified educational tokens. The project aims to make cause and effect in space systems understandable through play.
details:
Project Little Astronaut is an interactive 3D mission trainer for junior learners. Its learning loop is predict, act, observe, compare, and explain. At startup, a player can resume one of several saved attempts or start a new one. A short overview points to the real Habitat, Greenhouse, Storm shelter, and Research ridge in the game world. The first lesson explains Power, Air, Food, and Space Risk, asks a trial question, and guides the player to a station before free movement. Players use WASD or arrow keys to walk, E to interact, and Up/Down plus Enter, number keys, or a mouse click to choose an option.

Each committed station task advances one turn. Life support needs four power and the crew consumes one food token per turn. Crop lighting needs two consecutive powered turns to produce a harvest. Shelter reduces exposure; research uses extra power for science. The game explains changes after each action. Its replay compares another decision from the same starting state and forecast, while rewind lets the player continue from an earlier turn. The result clearly says Mission won or Mission lost, lists the specific safety conditions, and shows final resources, score, and rank. Scout, Commander, and Legend modes add more turns and strategic orders. Saved attempts, a leaderboard, optional crew play, a science handbook, and teach-back prompts support further exploration.

The game uses Godot 4.5.2 and GDScript, exports to WebGL 2, and is hosted with a Python account API on Azure App Service. A separate Python simulator checks the game rules. Authored NASA source cards cover life support, lunar power, crops, radiation, mission history, communication, and an archived DONKI solar-flare observation. The published flare is historical; the game's risk values, time steps, and scenarios are fictional learning rules, not NASA measurements. Local checks include 318 matching Godot/Python transitions, eight focused Python tests, and browser playthroughs covering both endings, replay, saves, and shared turns. Educational impact has not yet been measured with children.
